turns: My friend Arun Mehta borrowed Rs 2,00,000 from me last year and gave me a cheque dated 15 October 2026 to repay it. I deposited it on 20 October and my bank returned it on 27 October 2026 with the reason 'funds insufficient'. I got the return memo the same day. What should I do?

results.reply:
Arun ne aapko Rs 2,00,000 ka cheque diya tha, aapne 20 Oct ko deposit kiya aur 27 Oct ko bank ne ‘funds insufficient’ ke reason se return memo diya. Ab aapke paas 30 din ka window hai (till 26 Nov 2026) demand notice bhejne ka.

**What to do next**
- **Write a demand notice** under Sec 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. Mention cheque details, amount, date, return memo date, and ask Arun to pay the full amount within 15 days of receiving your notice.
- Send it by **registered post or speed‑post** and keep the receipt.
- If he pays within 15 days, case ends. If not, you can file a criminal complaint under Sec 142(1) of the same Act (within 1 month after the 15‑day period ends).

**Key points**
- Cheque was presented within its 3‑month validity (valid till 14 Jan 2027).
- You still have time to send the notice (20 days left).
- No lawyer needed for the notice; you can handle it yourself.

citations.title: Cheque bounce offence: conditions and punishment
citations.plain: Bouncing a cheque given to pay a legally enforceable debt, because of insufficient funds or because it exceeds the arranged limit, is a crime. Punishment is up to 2 years' jail, or a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both. The offence arises only if (a) the cheque was presented within its validity (now 3 months), (b) the payee sent a written demand notice within 30 days of learning it bounced, and (c) the drawer failed to pay within 15 days of receiving that notice.

citations.title: Time limit to file cheque bounce complaint
citations.plain: Only the payee or holder can file, by written complaint. It must be filed within one month after the cause of action arises, which is when the 15-day payment period after the notice ends without payment. A court can accept a late complaint if you show sufficient cause. Only a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class can try the case.

citations.title: Which court: territorial jurisdiction for cheque bounce (2015 amendment)
citations.plain: If you deposited the cheque through your bank account, file the case where your (the payee's) bank branch that maintains your account is located. If the cheque was presented other than through an account (e.g., over the counter), file where the drawer's bank branch is.

5. The cheque was presented within the statutory validity period of three months as per RBI guidelines.
6. The amount represented a legally enforceable debt arising from the loan given by me to Arun Mehta.

**Legal Basis:**
The dishonour of the cheque amounts to an offence under **Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881** ([NIA1881‑S138]).

**Demand:**
